video.title: Everyone’s Chasing AI. Start This Simple Business Instead

summary: Chris Koerner presents five low-capital businesses that sit around the hot tub industry rather than in hot tub manufacturing: hot tub inspection, custom spa covers, hot tub moving, hot tub rentals, and Airbnb hot tub cleaning/maintenance. Each is backed by case studies (mostly second-hand, found online or on Reddit) with revenue and pricing claims. He gives a validation playbook built on local Facebook groups, a Google Business Profile, a one-page website and cheap start-up. He closes by arguing that 'sweaty', non-AI businesses will gain demand as more people chase AI.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office; sells the TK Owners community

ideas.name: Airbnb hot tub cleaning and maintenance service
ideas.one_liner: Recurring weekly chemical balancing, drain-and-fill and repairs for hot tubs at short-term rentals.
ideas.business_model: Recurring weekly/monthly maintenance plans plus one-off service calls
ideas.customer: Airbnb / short-term rental owners and property managers with hot tubs
ideas.problem: Normal Airbnb cleaners do not know how to maintain hot tubs, yet a hot tub lets hosts charge $40-$100 more per night or is needed to compete.
ideas.offer: Hot tub cleaning, chemical balancing, drain and fill, with an Airbnb-level cleanliness guarantee

pricing.model: Per-visit weekly service, per-job drain and fill, monthly plans
pricing.notes: Hot tub adds roughly $1-2k/month booking income at 20 nights rented per the host's maths.

acquisition_channels.details: Reddit operator posted once in a local Facebook group, landed three clients in month one; host recommends sifting for the best 10-20% of local groups.

quote.text: he posted in a local Facebook group, landed three clients, and cleared over $3,000 in net profit
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Set up a Google Business Profile with photos, videos, five-star reviews, hours and website link.
Offer 50% off first jobs for a photo testimonial, or Amazon gift cards for referrals.
Simple one-page website; Austin got inbound demand with no paid ads.

ideas.delivery: Technicians physically visit each hot tub to balance chemicals, drain and fill and repair; Davis's firm scaled to 17 employees; chemicals bought in bulk.
unit_economics_claims: Reddit operator: 40 hot tubs per week grosses $7-8k per month
Davis (Chicago): 100+ units, over $1M annualised revenue, 17 employees in 3 years
Vermont company: 30-40 hot tubs a day, 4 days a week, $9-10k per week
Austin: first month MRR over $2,000 with about $1,000 chemicals and $750 website
ideas.startup_cost: Small: Austin about $750 website + a couple hundred for LLC + ~$1,000 chemicals; Reddit operator about $500 (logo $30, contract $250, hoses and chemicals $220); insurance $2-3k a year
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Within first month (Reddit operator landed clients in month one)

acquisition.how: Local Facebook group posting, GBP and a website can be tool-assisted, but group posting needs a human presence and cold DMs to individuals are restricted under PECR.

onboarding.how: Quotes, contracts and scheduling can be handled by forms and agents.

delivery.how: Physical on-site hot tub servicing every visit.

billing.how: Recurring subscription invoicing is easily automated.

support.how: Agents can handle scheduling and FAQ; callouts need humans.

uk_applicability.notes: Short-term rental market and hot tubs exist in the UK (Airbnb, holiday lets, Lake District, Cotswolds, Scotland); prices are in USD and need adapting, and public liability insurance and chemical handling rules apply. London/Bromley has fewer hot tub rentals, so a rural area is likely needed.

ideas.one_liner: Specialist movers for hot tubs, serving homeowners, retailers and spa companies.
ideas.customer: Hot tub retailers, spa companies, homeowners selling or moving

ideas.name: Custom hot tub covers via Shopify and Chinese print-on-demand
ideas.one_liner: Sell custom-design spa covers online and have Chinese manufacturers ship direct to customers.
ideas.business_model: One-off product sales with 4-5 year replacement cycle
ideas.customer: Hot tub owners needing replacement covers
ideas.problem: Existing covers get waterlogged, fall apart and do not fit well; slow delivery from competitors.
ideas.offer: Better or custom-designed hot tub covers with faster turnaround

acquisition_channels.details: Test 10-20 AI-generated designs with Facebook ads; shift budget to lowest cost per click.

quote.text: the ads that have the lowest cost per click I would start putting more budget towards
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.delivery: Order placed on Shopify, forwarded to Chinese manufacturer (Alibaba/AliExpress) which prints and ships directly; 3-week promised turnaround.
unit_economics_claims: Ocean Spa Covers (Babul) grew from $87.50 first order to multi-million dollar business
Spacovers.com founder shipped in two weeks vs competitors' four
ideas.startup_cost: Low: Shopify $39/month plus ad testing budget

acquisition.how: Paid ads and creative testing are agent-operable.

delivery.how: Supplier-fulfilled dropship; humans handle defects and sizing issues.

support.how: Agents handle tracking and returns; misprint disputes need people.

uk_applicability.notes: Shopify plus overseas manufacturing works in the UK, but customs duty, VAT and longer shipping times apply; UK suppliers may be better for fit and speed.

tactics.name: Validate through local Facebook groups
steps: Find multiple Facebook groups in each town and ignore the roughly 80% that are spammy
Spend time only in the 10-20% active, moderated groups
Post polls and feelers about demand for cleaning, covers, repairs, moving
Ask Airbnb owners what is breaking in their systems
Be upfront that you are testing and promise responsiveness, honesty and standing behind your work

quote.text: Find the 10 to 20% that are gold. Spend all your time in there and ignore everything else.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Referral-fee partnership with home inspectors
steps: Have the home inspector tell clients the hot tub is outside their scope
Inspector offers a $400 add-on
Inspector keeps $100 and passes $300 to you
Aligned incentives keep referrals flowing

tactics.name: Test hot tub demand with Airbnb hosts using data
steps: Ask hosts without a hot tub why competitors have them
Propose advertising the property with a hot tub for December
Compare bookings or price against last year and ask guests if the hot tub mattered
Use the result to sell rental or maintenance

tactics.name: Test cover designs with ads before buying stock
steps: Generate 10-20 designs with AI
List on a Shopify site
Run Facebook ads and push budget to lowest cost per click
Target LTV:CAC of 5:1
Order one-by-one from Chinese manufacturer shipping direct to customers
Capture email and phone for 4-5 year replacement reminders

tactics.name: Gradual pivot by asking customers a new question
steps: On inbound moving calls, ask if they also have a hot tub
Offer to beat competing quote (e.g. $450 vs $500)
Shift niche focus gradually

tactics.name: Cheap start discipline
steps: Do not incorporate until you have customers
Start small, under-buy chemicals and materials
Track all expenses in Google Sheets
Use a personal account at first, upgrade to QuickBooks or Xero when rolling
Buy insurance (about $2-3k/year)

tactics.name: Get first reviews and testimonials
steps: Set up Google Business Profile with photos, videos and hours
Do first jobs free or at 50% off for photo testimonials
Offer Amazon gift cards for referrals
Build one-page website with phone, form, services and pricing

quote.text: Pay up for insurance. It's going to cost 2 to three grand a year.

warnings.warning: Check whether hot tubs actually exist in your climate and market before launching.

lessons.lesson: Look for businesses around an industry, not in it; adjacent service niches are cheaper and more approachable than manufacturing.

quote.text: the opportunity is not in the hot tub industry itself. It's in what happens after someone buys a hot tub
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Specialist niches beat generalists: generalists refuse or exclude awkward items, and specialists can charge a premium.
Recurring revenue with aligned incentives (Airbnb income uplift) makes a service business sticky and valuable.
Speed of delivery can be a competitive moat even without better quality (two weeks versus four for spa covers).
Validate demand cheaply (polls, local groups, ads) before buying equipment or incorporating.
Pivot gradually by changing how you talk to customers rather than burning the boats.

quote.text: A pivot is usually gradual and slow.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: As AI draws entrepreneurs, supply of non-AI 'sweaty' services may fall and prices rise.

quote.text: AI is not going to lift that hot tub off the deck. It's never going to do that.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Customer lifetime value justifies spending up on acquisition; target LTV:CAC of about 5:1.
Being first mover locally (SEO, Google profile) can dominate small niche markets.

evidence_quality.rationale: Listicle of second-hand case studies found online and on Reddit; figures are unverified, some projected, and some prices appear mis-transcribed. Few first-hand details beyond the host's tree-trimming anecdote and an Airbnb cleaner interview with no figures.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Host sells TK Owners community ($99/month), uses a Bizzy referral link, and the video includes a HighLevel sponsor read.
